combinations.name: Alcohol & CNS depressants
combinations.description: Sedation and respiratory depression add up, and ketamine's dissociation makes it hard to notice either happening. Nausea and vomiting are also more likely — a real problem if you can't protect your airway. If combining at all, keep both doses low and don't dose alone.

combinations.name: Stimulants
combinations.description: The stimulant masks ketamine's sedation, so doses that would have put you down feel manageable — until the stimulant fades first and the full dissociative load lands at once. Judge the ketamine dose as if the stimulant weren't there.
